Stay Safe

Precautions for buyers & sellers

Property fraud is real in Pakistan. Follow these precautions — in line with the checklists issued by development authorities and Pakistan's leading property portals — before you pay anyone a single rupee.

For buyers

  • Verify the scheme's approval. Ask for the final approval letter and approved layout plan from the relevant authority (LDA, CDA, MDA…). Confirm your plot lies inside the approved area and is not mortgaged to the authority.
  • Check ownership documents. Fard, registry or allotment letter — and verify them online (PLRA for Punjab, the Sindh land records portal). For big deals, hire a property lawyer.
  • Pay token money only to the owner. The person whose name and CNIC appear on the transfer letter — never to a dealer “acting as owner”. Always take a written agreement.
  • No advance without verification. Never pay cash without proper receipts; check pending utility bills and society dues first.
  • Visit the property in person. Confirm it exists, matches the documents, and is not on public utility land (parks, schools, graveyards).
  • Watch the red flags. Missing documents, a seller who won't show originals, ownership disputes, fake NOCs, double registration, or pressure tactics like “rates go up tonight” — walk away.

For sellers

  • Verify the buyer's identity. Check the original CNIC and keep copies of every document exchanged.
  • Use banking channels. Pay orders and bank transfers only — avoid large cash deals without signed receipts.
  • Originals only against payment. Never hand over original documents before the full amount is verified in your account.
  • Get everything in writing. Token receipts and sale agreements with clear payment timelines protect both sides.
  • Verify bank instruments. Confirm pay orders and drafts with the issuing bank before transferring anything — fake instruments are a classic scam.
  • Prefer verified agents. PakZameen verified agencies pass CNIC and office verification — look for the badge.

Spotted suspected fraud on PakZameen? Report it to us — and always do your own verification. PakZameen lists properties but does not guarantee any transaction.
